STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

TABATABAI:25:41-62/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-62/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:25:41-62/r1.claim: The quoted Prophetic report, introduced just before this segment as transmitted from Abu Umama, says the greatest deity worshipped under heaven besides God is a desire that is followed.
TABATABAI:25:41-62/r1.anchor: ما تحت ظل السماء من إله يعبد من دون الله أعظم عند الله من هوى متبع

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.claim: A person enslaved to desire exceeds natural limits and becomes worse than an animal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.anchor: he crosses all limits of his instincts and nature

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r1.claim: Hawā is the soul’s spontaneous inclination and bare preference.

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r2.claim: Placing the second object first conveys restriction: they recognize no deity beyond what their desire dictates.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r2.anchor: ikinci mef‘ûlün takdim olunması kasr ifade etmek içindir ki, canının istediğinden başka kendine ilâh tanımayan demektir.

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r3.claim: Such people have no devotion to truth and are simply self-seeking.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r3.anchor: Böyle kimselerde hiç hak perestişi yok, sade bir hodgâmlık vardır.

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r4.claim: They worship pleasure, disregard proof and rights, and sacrifice truth even when they know their pleasure brings ruin; they reduce religion to personal sensation and refuse God’s pleasure.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r4.anchor: Dini de insanın mücerred hissiyâtından, yani sadece keyif ve zevkinden ibaret tanırlar.

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r5.speaker: Ebû Ümâme
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r5.claim: A report attributed to Abu Umama says that among objects worshiped besides God, followed desire is the greatest in God’s sight.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r5.anchor: Ebû Ümâme radıyallâhu anh’tan tahric etmişlerdir, demiş ki:

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r6.claim: The first question is confirmatory, while the second denies that the Prophet can be their guardian or rescue them.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r6.anchor: Evvelki istifham takrîrî, bu istifham inkârîdir. Yani gördün a ona vekil olamazsın, üzerine müvekkel olup da kurtaramazsın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r1.claim: People assess a message either through reason, weighing its truth and significance before accepting or rejecting it, or through desires, bodily pleasures, passing wants, and petty interests.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r1.anchor: İnsan, kendisine hitap eden bir mesajı değerlendirirken ya aklına ya da arzu ve ihtiraslarının buyruğuna uyar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.claim: The Qur'an opposes the mindset that deifies base desires; while people persist in it, they cannot understand the Prophet's call or reason soundly and are more astray than animals.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.anchor: putperestlerin, bayağı arzularını tanrı edinmeyi sürdürdükçe Peygamber’in davetini doğru anlamalarının, akıllarını kullanarak sağlıklı değerlendirme yapmalarının imkânsız olduğu bildirilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.claim: These verses criticize Meccan polytheists while teaching a universal lesson: across history, people wrongly rank bodily desires, material interests, and status above reason, sound belief, and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.anchor: insanlığın temel sorunu, bedensel arzularını, maddî çıkarlarını, makam ve mevki tutkularını akıl ve irfanın ışığından, doğru inanç ve sağlıklı düşünceden, hak ve adalet ölçülerine göre hüküm ve karar verip hayatlarını bu ölçülerle düzenlemekten daha önemli görmeleridir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.claim: The Moses and Noah narratives and intervening peoples assure the Prophet and warn his nation: earlier communities mocked messengers who taught them and ultimately suffered a terrible fate; the next sūrah gives these events in detail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.anchor: The purpose is to assure the Prophet (sws) and warn his nation that God sent His teachings to these nations as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r3.claim: The address form used here is discussed at another point in the exegesis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r3.anchor: style of address has been discussed at an appropriate instance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.claim: These verses reassure the Prophet: intellect guides, while desire enslaves, and those who abandon intellect cannot be guided.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.anchor: It is a person’s intellect that guides him and not his desire. None can guide people who forsake their intellect and become slaves of their desire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r5.claim: Desires are blind and seek only their own fulfillment, without regard for good or evil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r5.anchor: These desires only want their demands to be fulfilled. They are not concerned with good or evil.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r6.claim: Whoever makes desire a god becomes caught in Satan’s web in a way that is almost impossible to escape.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r6.anchor: a way that they become his god gets entangled in the web weaved by Satan to such an extent that it become impossible for him to escape from it.

QASHANI:25:43-46/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:43-46/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:43-46/r1.claim: Anyone veiled by something and stopping with it loves and resembles it, and thus truly worships passion through worship of that beloved.

QASHANI:25:43-46/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:43-46/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:43-46/r2.claim: Satan prompts love of things besides God; loving anything for its own sake makes one worship the beloved, one’s passion, and Satan, dividing one’s orientation among gods.
QASHANI:25:43-46/r2.anchor: والباعث لهواه على محبة غير الله هو الشيطان

QASHANI:25:43-46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:43-46/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:43-46/r3.claim: A person already veiled by a shadow of God is far removed, so the Prophet cannot be their guardian by calling them to unity.
QASHANI:25:43-46/r3.anchor: بدعوته إلى التوحيد وقد كان في غاية البعد محجوبا بظل من ظلاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r3.claim: The question about one who makes desire his god signals despair of their believing and tells the Messenger not to grieve; their ignorance of benefit and consequences is like that of animals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r3.anchor: هذا يأس عن إيمانهم وإشارة إليه عليه السلام أن لا يتأسف عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r5.claim: In اتخذ, إلهه is the first object and هواه the second: the person makes nothing but his desire a deity; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the قلب analysis as awkward, since it requires reversing the phrase and relies on poetic license.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r5.anchor: وإلهه المفعول الأول لاتخذ، وهواه الثاني أي أقام مقام الإله الذي يعبده هواه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r6.claim: A man would worship an idol, then cast it aside for a more attractive one when he saw it, illustrating worship governed by desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r6.anchor: كان الرجل يعبد الصنم فإذا رأى أحسن منه رماه وأخذ الأحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r7.claim: The verse is said to concern al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who worshipped whatever he desired; hawa means the heart’s inclination toward something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r7.anchor: قيل: نزلت في الحارث بن قيس السهمي، كان إذا هوي شيئا عبده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r8.claim: The question أفأنت تجبره asks whether the Messenger can force him to abandon desire or protect him from his profound ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r8.anchor: أفأنت تجبره على ترك هواه، أو أفأنت تحفظه من عظيم جهله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r9.speaker: بعض أهل المدينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r9.claim: Some Medinan readers read من اتخذ آلهة with a plural and tanwin, construing desire as varied kinds and each kind as a different deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ بعض أهل المدينة من اتخذ آلهة منونة على الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r10.speaker: ابن هرمز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r10.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads إلاهة, taking the phrase to mean that his desire is a worshipped object; the feminine ending intensifies the sense, so the word is declinable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز: إلاهة على وزن فعالة وفيه أيضا تقديم أي هواه إلاهة بمعنى معبود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r11.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r11.claim: An alternative explanation takes الإلاهة as the sun, also called ألاهة; although normally diptote as a feminine proper name, it is declinable here because some dialects use the article with it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: بل الإلاهة الشمس ويقال لها ألاهة بضم الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r12.claim: For أرأيت, من is the first object and the interrogative clause is the second; وكيلا asks whether the Messenger can call the person to guidance, entrust him to God, and compel him to Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r12.anchor: ومفعول أرأيت الأول هو من والجملة الاستفهامية في موضع المفعول الثاني

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r1.claim: Taking desire as a god means obeying it and making it the basis of one's religion, without hearing proof or seeing evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r1.anchor: بأن أطاعه وبنى عليه دينه لا يسمع حجة ولا يبصر دليلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r2.claim: The second object is advanced for emphasis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r2.anchor: وإنما قدم المفعول الثاني للعناية به

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r3.claim: The first question expresses confirmation and astonishment; the second denies that the Prophet could guard such a person from idolatry and sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r3.anchor: فالاستفهام الأول للتقرير والتعجيب والثاني للإنكار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r1.claim: Taking one's desire as a god means devoting oneself to worshipping desire, leaving no path to righteousness; reversing the word order would make desire subordinate to God instead.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r1.anchor: ولو قيل : من اتخذ هواه إلهه , لكان المعنى أنه قصر هواه على الإله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the verse to mean that the man has taken no god except his desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r2.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والمعنى أنه لم يتخذ إلها إلا هواه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r3.claim: Word order changes meaning: making a servant one's father elevates the servant, whereas making one's father a servant demeans him; similarly, the verse's order makes desire the sole object of worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r3.anchor: فلان اتخذ عبده أباه , لكان معناه أنه عظم العبد , ولو قيل : إنه اتخذ اباه عبده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r4.claim: The Prophet cannot act as a divinely appointed guardian who compels a person away from desire; he is responsible only for conveying the message, so he should not grieve himself over them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r4.anchor: لست بوكيل , ولكنك رسول , ليس عليك إلا البلاغ , فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r1.claim: In pre-Islamic times a man might worship a white stone, then discard it for a better-looking one; the verse was revealed about this practice.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} قال: كان الرجل يعبد الحجر الأبيض زمانا من الدهر

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r2.claim: Abū Rajāʾ describes people who ate blood with al-ʿilḥiz and worshipped stones, changing idols for better ones and announcing when an idol was lost; the verse was revealed about them.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r2.anchor: عن أبي رجاء العطاردي قال: كانوا في الجاهلية يأكلون الدم بالعلهز ويعبدون الحجر

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses taking desire as a god as following whatever one desires.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} قال: لا يهوى شيئا إلا تبعه

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r4.claim: Qatāda says such a person does whatever he wants and whatever he craves, restrained by neither piety nor God-consciousness.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} قال: كلما هوى شيئا ركبه وكلما اشتهى شيئا أتاه

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says there is polytheism among Muslims: an idolater bows to sun or moon, while a hypocrite submits to his own desire.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r5.anchor:
عن الحسن أنه قيل له: في أهل القبلة شرك فقال: نعم
المنافق مشرك إن المشرك يسجد للشمس

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r6.claim: The Prophet says no deity worshipped under the sky besides God is greater in God's sight than a desire one follows.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r6.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تحت ظل السماء من إله يعبد من دون الله أعظم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r7.claim: The reminder about one who makes desire his god consoles the Prophet: he should not grieve over their disbelief or expect sound judgment from them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r7.anchor: ثم أنس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن كفرهم بقوله أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r10.claim: Taking desire as a god means making desire obeyed; desire leads to corruption because the soul commands evil, while soundness comes from obeying reason.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r10.anchor: معناه جعل هواه مطاعا فصار كالإله والهوى قائد إلى كل فساد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says desire itself is the god worshipped apart from God; al-Thaʿlabī transmits this view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس الهوى الإله يعبد من دون الله ذكره الثعلبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r12.claim: Another explanation is that they worshipped stones, replacing an idol with a more attractive one whenever their preference changed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r12.anchor: وقيل الإشارة بقوله إلهه هواه إلى ما كانوا عليه من أنهم كانوا يعبدون حجرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r13.speaker: الأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r13.claim: Al-Aʿraj is reported to read ilāhahu hawāhu, explaining that desire takes the sun as a light by which it is guided; the sun may be called ilāha and inflected either way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r13.anchor: قال أبو حاتم وروي عن رجل من أهل المدينة قال ابن جني هو الأعرج إلهه هواه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r14.claim: A wakīl is the person who takes charge of a matter and undertakes it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r14.anchor: و «الوكيل» القائم على الأمر الناهض به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r1.claim: One who takes desire as a god makes whatever he likes and deems good the basis of his religion; 35:8 is a parallel, and the Prophet is not appointed as that person’s guardian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r1.anchor: {أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} أي: مهما استحسن من شيء ورآه حسنا في هوى نفسه، كان دينه ومذهبه، كما قال تعالى: {أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات} [فاطر:8] ؛ ولهذا قال هاهنا: {أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا} .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas illustrates pagan caprice with a man worshipping a white stone, then replacing it with another he finds more beautiful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية يعبد الحجر الأبيض زمانا، فإذا رأى غيره أحسن منه عبد الثاني وترك الأول.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r1.claim: A person who follows desire in religion without considering evidence or listening to proof makes desire his god and worships it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r1.anchor: من كان في طاعة الهوى في دينه يتبعه في كل ما يأتي ويذر لا يتبصر دليلا ولا يصغي إلى برهان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r2.claim: The Prophet is asked rhetorically how he could guide or compel someone who recognizes no object of worship but desire, since he is no coercive guardian over them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r2.anchor: كيف تستطيع أن تدعوه إلى الهدى أفتتوكل عليه وتجبره على الإسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r3.claim: It is reported that idolaters worshipped stones, but when a more attractive stone appeared they discarded the first and took another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r3.anchor: ويروى أن الرجل منهم كن يعبد الحجر ، فإذا رأى أحسن منه رمى به وأخذ آخر .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p287/r4.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Sahmī was one of these people who followed desire.

NAHHAS:v3p161/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r12.claim: The question means: are you to compel him to do so?
NAHHAS:v3p161/r12.anchor: قيل معناه أفأنت تجبره على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r1.claim: “Have you seen?” can introduce information or a question; here it expresses astonishment at the ignorance of the person described.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r1.anchor: الأول : قوله : { أرأيت } كلمة تصلح للإعلام والسؤال ، وههنا هي تعجيب من جهل من هذا وصفه ونعته

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r2.claim: The phrase means he made his desire the object of worship, or a deity he desires; taking it as an inversion is weak because the actual wording conveys exclusivity.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r2.anchor: وقيل هو مقلوب ومعناه اتخذ هواه إلهه وهذا ضعيف ، لأن قوله : { اتخذ إلاهه هواه } يفيد الحصر

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that desire itself is a god that is worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الهوى إله يعبد

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says a polytheist would worship an idol, then replace it with a more attractive one when he saw it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : كان الرجل من المشركين يعبد الصنم فإذا رأى أحسن منه رماه واتخذ الآخر وعبده

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r5.claim: “Guardian over him” means one who protects him from following his desire; Muhammad is not such a guardian.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r5.anchor: أي حافظا تحفظه من اتباع هواه أي لست كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r6.claim: Razi links this denial of coercive control to verses saying the Messenger is not an overseer or enforcer and there is no compulsion in religion.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r6.anchor: وقوله : { لا إكراه فى الدين } ( البقرة : 256 ) قال الكلبي : نسختها آية القتال

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r7.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse “there is no compulsion in religion” was abrogated by the fighting verse.

TABATABAI:25:43-44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r1.claim: The preceding statement about taking desire as god is summarized by the verse about being unable to make those in graves hear, and elaborated in the verse about one who makes desire his god and is sealed from guidance.
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r1.anchor: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

TABATABAI:25:43-44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r2.claim: The natural syntax makes ilahahu the first object of ittakhadha and hawahu the second: they rightly recognize an obeyed deity but wrongly make desire, rather than truth, their authority.
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r2.anchor: أي إن { اتخذ } فعل متعد إلى مفعولين

TABATABAI:25:43-44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r3.speaker: عدة من المفسرين
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r3.claim: A number of commentators instead make hawahu the first object and ilahahu the delayed second object, explaining the order as emphasis or exclusivity; Tabatabai rejects this as ill-suited to the context.
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r3.anchor: أن { هواه } مفعول أول لقوله { اتخذ } و { إلهه } مفعول ثان مقدم

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r2.claim: One report says a pagan worshipped a stone, then abandoned it for a better-looking stone he passed and worshipped that instead.
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r2.anchor: فإذا مر بحجر أحسن منه ترك الأول وعبد الثاني

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r3.claim: Another explanation says they make desire their god by obeying and following it without caring about the consequences.
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r3.anchor: أي أطاع هواه وركبه فلم يبال عاقبة ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r4.claim: وكيلا means a guardian or custodian.

TABRISI:25:43-45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:25:43-45/r1.claim: A polytheist would worship a stone idol, then discard it and worship a better-looking one when he saw it.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r1.anchor: وكان الرجل من المشركين يعبد الحجر والصنم فإذا رأى أحسن منه رمى به وأخذه يعبد الآخر عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:25:43-45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r2.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:25:43-45/r2.claim: The person abandons worship of the Creator and makes a stone his god; this is reported from Ibn Abbas.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r2.anchor: من ترك عبادة خالقه وإلهه هو حجر فعبده ما حاله عندك عن عطاء عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:25:43-45/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r3.speaker: القتيبي
TABRISI:25:43-45/r3.claim: Following and obeying one's desire makes it like a god, while the person abandons the truth.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r3.anchor: من أطاع هواه واتبعه فهو كالإله له وترك الحق عن القتيبي

TABRISI:25:43-45/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:43-45/r4.claim: The Prophet cannot act as guardian to protect such a person from following desire and worshipping what he desires.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r4.anchor: لأن الوكيل هو الكافي للشيء ولا يكون كذلك إلا وهو قادر عليه

TABRISI:25:43-45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:25:43-45/r5.claim: Alternatively, the question asks whether Muhammad can guide someone who neither reflects nor considers; he cannot, since a guardian must be capable of what he undertakes.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r5.anchor: أتقدر أنت يا محمد أن تهديه إذا لم يتدبر ولم يتفكر أي لا تقدر على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r9.claim: Rāzī explains their rejection as the domination of imitation and desire: they follow whatever inclination urges, whether or not evidence forbids it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r9.anchor: بلوغ هؤلاء في جهالتهم وإعراضهم عن الدلائل إنما كان لاستيلاء التقليد عليهم

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r1.claim: “Have you seen?” can introduce information or a question; here it expresses astonishment.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r1.anchor: كلمة أرأيت تستعمل تارة للإعلام وتارة للسؤال وههنا للتعجيب

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r2.claim: The second object, “his god,” precedes the first for emphasis because it is the focus of the astonishment.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r2.anchor: وإلهه مفعولة ثان قدم على الأول للاعتناء به لأنه الذي يدور عليه أمر التعجب

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r3.claim: Hawāʾ first meant what one loves or desires, then the desired object; usage came to associate it especially with blameworthy desire.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r3.anchor: والهوى مصدر هويه إذا أحبه واشتهاه ثم سمي به المهوى المشتهى محمودا كان أو مذموما ثم غلب على غير المحمود

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r4.claim: Hawāʾ is what temperament inclines toward and the soul craves merely from desire, without transmitted authority or rational proof.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r4.anchor: فالهوى ما يميل إليه الطبع وتهواه النفس بمجرد الاشتهاء من غير سند منقول ودليل معقول.

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r5.claim: A person makes desire a god by obeying it and building religion on it while rejecting all proof; the question calls for astonishment.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى أرأيت يا محمد من جعل هواه إلها لنفسه بأن أطاعه وبنى عليه أمر دينه معرضا عن استماع الحجة والبرهان بالكلية

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r6.claim: A Persian anecdote says some Arabs worshipped stones they found attractive, discarding an old idol when they found a better one; it names Ḥārith ibn Qays among them.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r6.anchor: (وكفته أند قومي بودند ازعرب كه سنك مي رستيدند هركاهكه ايشانرا سنكي نيكو بجشم آمدي ودل ايشان آن خواستي

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r7.claim: A hadith states that no deity is more hateful to God than desire.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ما عبد إله أبغض على الله من الهوى"

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r8.claim: The Najmiyya reading says whoever loves something other than God and becomes occupied with it is worshipping his own desire, which prefers that object to God.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r8.anchor: فهو عابد هواه كما في "التأويلات النجمية".

BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r9.speaker: سيد حسني رحمه الله
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r9.claim: Sayyid Ḥasanī’s Tarab al-majālis traces human desire to the union of Iblīs and the world, whose effects produce rejected customs and diverse religions.
BURSEVI:v6p157#2/r9.anchor: سيد حسني رحمه الله در طرب المجالس أورده كه ون آدم صفي عليه السلام باحوا عقد بستند إبليس ودنيا بيكديكر يوستند

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r1.claim: The saying “desire was the first god worshipped on earth” makes false deities branches of desire; resisting desire leads to true faith.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r1.anchor: "الهوى أول إله عبد في الأرض" درشان أو واردشده وزبان قرآن درحق اونين فرموده

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان رحمه الله
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r2.claim: Abū Sulaymān says following desire kills the self: remembrance is its life, heedlessness its death, and heedlessness leads to passions and the state of the dead.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو سليمان رحمه الله : من أتبع نفسه هواها فقد سعى في قتلها لأن حياتها بالذكر وموتها وقتلها بالغفلة

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r3.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r3.claim: The Mathnawī contrasts prophets and unbelievers in the same worldly marketplace: lust traps both, but believers are genuine gold and unbelievers counterfeit.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r3.anchor:
وفي "المثنوي" :
اين جهان شهوتي يتخانة ايست
انبيا وكافرانرا لأنه ايست

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r4.speaker: أكابر
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r4.claim: An interpretation attributed to elders says dreaming that the Prophet has died signifies weakness or deficiency in the dreamer’s religious practice; losing divine presence is analogous.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r4.anchor: أكابر كفته اندكه اكركسي درخواب بيندكه يغمبر صلى الله عليه وسلم مرده است تعبيرش آنست كه درشريعت اين صاحب واقعة قصوري وفتوري

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r5.speaker: جامي رحمه الله
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r5.claim: Jāmī offers another reading: the dreamed-of “god” is a desire the person had worshipped; its disappearance from the heart signals increased presence with God.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r5.anchor: ومولانا نور الدين عبد الرحمن جامي رحمه الله اين سخن را تأويل ديكر كرده بودند

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r6.claim: “Against him” refers to the person who has made his desire a god; wakīl means a guardian protecting him from idolatry and sins.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r6.anchor: {عليه} (برآنكس كه هواي خودرا خدا ساخته) {وكيلا} حفيظا تمنعه عن الشرك والمعاصي

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r7.claim: The question denies that the Prophet is charged with guarding such a person; his task is warning, not being his keeper.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r7.anchor: لست موكلا على حفظه بل أنت منذر فهذا الاستفهام للإنكار

BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r8.claim: The rhetorical denial does not forbid calling them; it tells the Prophet he has completed warning and removing excuses.
BURSEVI:v6p157#3/r8.anchor: وليس هذا نهيا عن دعائه إياهم بل الإعلام بأنه قد قضى ما عليه من الإنذار والأعذار

STUDYQURAN:25:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r1.speaker: Aj, Z
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r1.claim: Idolaters obey their passions so fully that they worship them.
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r1.anchor: The idolaters obey their passions to the point of worshipping them (Aj, Z).

STUDYQURAN:25:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r2.speaker: some commentators (Aj, Q, R)
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r2.claim: Some report that fickle idolaters would abandon an idol for another they found better or more beautiful.
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r2.anchor: some were so fickle that, upon seeing a better or more beautiful idol than the one they were worshipping, they would quickly abandon the first

STUDYQURAN:25:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r3.speaker: Aj, Q
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r3.claim: Those ruled by impulse and passion cannot be persuaded by the Prophet to worship the One God.
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r3.anchor: those who act on impulse and respond to their passions cannot be persuaded to worship the One God (Aj, Q).

STUDYQURAN:25:43/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r4.claim: The verse connects with the reminder that the Prophet is not a warder over them.
STUDYQURAN:25:43/r4.anchor: See also 88:22: Thou art not a warder over them.

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.claim: The passage gathers traits matching the disbelievers' objections: mocking the Messenger, following desire, worshipping what cannot harm or benefit, and refusing to prostrate to God.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.anchor: مما يناسب سنخ اعتراضاتهم واقتراحاتهم كاستهزائهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r8.claim: Hawā is the soul's inclination toward desire when reason does not moderate it.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r8.anchor: الهوى ميل النفس إلى الشهوة من غير تعديله بالعقل

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r9.claim: Taking desire as a god means obeying and following it instead of God; the Qur'an often condemns following desire and calls obedience to another being worship.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r9.anchor: والمراد باتخاذ الهوى إلها طاعته واتباعه من دون الله

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r10.claim: The question is a rebuke that denies the Prophet is responsible for managing or guiding this person to right conduct; he cannot do so after God has let him stray and cut off guidance.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r10.anchor: استفهام إنكاري أي لست أنت وكيلا عليه قائما على نفسه وباموره

TABRISI:25:41-42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r3.speaker: الأعرج
TABRISI:25:41-42/r3.claim: In an anomalous reading, al-Aʿraj reads “the sun” (al-ilāha) for “his god.”
TABRISI:25:41-42/r3.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة الأعرج من اتخذ الألاهة هواه

TABRISI:25:41-42/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r4.claim: Al-ilāha means the sun; the form alāha with ḍamma is indeclinable, and the cited poem uses al-alāha for the sun.
TABRISI:25:41-42/r4.anchor: وقيل: ألهة بالضم غير مصروفة وأنشد: تروحنا من اللعباء عصرا

TABRISI:25:41-42/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r5.claim: A reading “and your deity” can mean your worship; it may also mean the sun worshipped by the addressee, like saying “your sun.”
TABRISI:25:41-42/r5.anchor: ومن قرأ وألهتك فمعناه وعبادتك وقد يجوز أن يكون أراد هذه المعرفة فأضافها إليه لعبادته لها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r1.claim: The person recognizes God as deity and creator, yet desires and worships a stone; the verse asks his standing before God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: أرأيت يا محمد من عرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r2.claim: Arabs sometimes worshipped whatever they desired, replacing a stone or tree with a better-looking one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كانت العرب إذا هوى الرجل منهم شيئا عبده من دون الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r3.claim: In pre-Islamic practice one might worship a stone, then replace it with a better one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كان أهل الجاهلية يعبد أحدهم الحجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r4.claim: Muqātil identifies the example as al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Sahmī, who worshipped a stone he desired.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وذلك أن الحارث بن قيس السهمي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r5.claim: Possible parses supply an omitted preposition or make the god whatever he desires, naming the object by the verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r5.anchor: تقدير الآية: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه بهواه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r6.claim: The cited line uses hawā for inclination or desire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r6.anchor: هوى بتهامة وهوى بنجد ... فما أدري أنجد أم أغور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r7.claim: The verse expresses astonishment at their ignorance in worshipping what desire leads them to; desire leads to falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r7.anchor: ومعنى الآية: تعجيب النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- من نهاية جهلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ selects the interpretation that desire led them to worship an idol.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r9.claim: Another view takes hawā as an idol worshipped besides God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r9.anchor: وهو قول الحسن وابن عباس؛ قال ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says such a person follows whatever he desires.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا يهوى شيئا إلا اتبعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the second view as obeying and following desire without regard for consequences.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r11.anchor: فقال في القول الثاني: أي: أطاع هواه، وركبه فلم يبال عاقبة ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the person follows desire, abandons truth, and treats desire like a god.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p511#2/r12.anchor: وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة؛ قال: يقول: يتبع هواه ويدع الحق فهو كالإله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r1.claim: The Prophet is not a controller over him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لست عليه بمسيطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r2.claim: The Prophet does not control the person's choice to follow desire and error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يريد أن تكون بيدك المشيئة في الهوى والضلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r3.claim: The Prophet cannot guard someone from following desire and worshipping what he desires instead of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أفأنت عليه حافظ، تحفظه من اتباع هواه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p513/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse was abrogated by the fighting verse.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r8.claim: They worshipped whatever their desire chose: if they saw a more attractive stone, they discarded the first idol for it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r8.anchor: كانوا يعبدون شيئا حجرا، أو ما كان، فإذا رأوا حجرا أحسن طرحوا الأول وعبدوا الأحسن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r9.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for making such a person believe; his duty is only to deliver the message.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r9.anchor: حفيظا حتى ترده إلى الإيمان، أي: ليس عليك إلا التبليغ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r10.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r10.claim: It is also said that this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا مما نسخته آية السيف

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the person who makes desire a god as a hypocrite who acts on every desire.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r5.anchor: حدثني المبارك بن فضالة، عن الحسن قال: هو المنافق يصيب هواه، كلما هوى شيئا فعله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r6.claim: Yaḥyā also identifies the person as a polytheist.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r7.claim: A guardian would watch the person’s deeds until requiting him; Muḥammad is a warner, not a lord.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r7.anchor: على الذي اتخذ إلهه هواه. {وكيلا} [الفرقان: 43] حفيظا تحفظ عليه عمله حتى تجازيه به.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r8.claim: Al-Suddī explains wakīl as one who dominates or controls.

BURHAN:v3p277/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p277/r1.claim: In the phrase about taking desire as a god, the usual order would put desire before its predicate; the second object is advanced for emphasis, as when one says I knew departing, Zayd.
BURHAN:v3p277/r1.anchor: وأصل الكلام هواه إلهه كما تقول اتخذ الصنم معبودا

BURHAN:v3p427/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p427/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p427/r5.claim: The syntax makes desire stronger and more binding for the person than his supposed deity by placing desire in the position of the god.
BURHAN:v3p427/r5.anchor: فإنه جعل المفعول الأول ثانيا والثاني أولا للتنبيه على أن الهوى أقوى وأوثق عنده

SULAMI:v2p61#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r1.claim: Following the ego's desires is like joining in killing it: remembrance gives it life, heedlessness kills it, and desire makes it among the dead.
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان : من اتبع نفسه هواها فقد اشرك في قتلها لأن حياتهما بالذكر ،

SULAMI:v2p61#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r2.claim: The ego lives while opposing its desires and dies when it follows them, through immersion in sins and turning from obedience.
SULAMI:v2p61#3/r2.anchor: قال أيضا : النفس حية ما دامت تخالف هواها فإذا وافقت هواها ماتت ، وموتها في انهماكها في المعاصي

ITQAN:v3p34/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p34/r1.claim: In “who takes his desire as his god,” the default order is “his desire as his god”; the second object is fronted for emphasis.
ITQAN:v3p34/r1.anchor: والأصل ( هواه إلهه ) لأن من اتخذ إلهه هواه غير مذموم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r1.claim: A generic predicate such as «the brave is protected» distributes the quality across the whole class of brave people.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r1.anchor: المعنى في قولك : الشجاع موقى ، أنك تثبت الوقاية لكل ذات من صفتها الشجاعة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r2.claim: By contrast, «you are the brave one» does not gather every brave person into one; it presents the addressee as the complete, unqualified embodiment of bravery.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p155/r2.anchor: حتى إذا صرنا إلى المخاطب وجدناه قد استكمل هذه الصفة ، واستجمع شرائطها ، وأخلص جوهرها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303/r1.claim: Metaphorical eloquence comes from the subtlety and novelty of the transfer in meaning: the metaphor leaves the word’s letters and sounds unchanged, so its effect is semantic.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p303/r1.anchor: اللفظ المستعار إذا كان فصيحا كانت فصاحته تلك من أجل استعارته ومن أجل لطف وغرابة كانا فيها

DAMGHANI:v1p493/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r14.claim: وكيل can mean one who controls or dominates others; this is the sense of the question about the one who follows desire.
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r14.anchor: الثالث الوكيل الممسيطر قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام وما أنت عليهم بوكيل يعني بمسيطر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r5.claim: A third sense is controller or one who has authority over another.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الوكيل في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r1.claim: The person follows his desire and abandons the truth, making desire for him like a god.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r1.anchor: {أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} يقول: يتبع هواه ويدع الحق، فهو له كالإله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r2.claim: Wakīl means guarantor; another gloss is guardian.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#5/r2.anchor: {أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا} أي كفيلا. وقيل: حافظا.

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r1.claim: The two objects of ittakhadha remain in their stated order because both are equally definite.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r1.anchor: مفعولا الاتخاذ من غير تقديم ولا تأخير لاستوائهما في التعريف

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says hawāhu is advanced for emphasis, comparing it to “I knew Zayd as departing.”
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r2.anchor: ما هو إلا تقديم المفعول الثاني على الأول للعناية به

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r3.claim: The Shaykh objects that calling this inversion is improper because such inversion belongs to poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r3.anchor: وادعاء القلب يعني التقديم ليس بجيد لأنه من ضرائر الأشعار

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r4.claim: The author rejects that objection: this is merely preposing and postposing, not the disputed poetic “inversion.”
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r4.anchor: على أن هذا ليس من القلب المذكور في شيء، إنما هو تقديم وتأخير فقط

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r5.speaker: ابن هرمز
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r5.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads ilāhata hawāhu on the faʿāla pattern; ilāhah means the worshiped one, with an intensive hāʾ, and is the indefinite second object placed first.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز " إلاهة هواه " على وزن فعالة. والإهة بمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r6.claim: Some explain ilāhah here as the sun; the author objects that a proper feminine name should be diptote, while the counterargument says it often takes al- and becomes an indefinite adjective when stripped of it.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r6.anchor: وقيل: الإهة هي الشمس. ورد هذا: بأنه كان ينبغي أن يمتنع من الصرف

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r7.claim: The name for the sun is also attested as alāhah, with ḍamma on the initial hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r7.anchor: ويقال: ألاهة بضم الهمزة أيضا اسما للشمس

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r8.speaker: بعض المدنيين
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r8.claim: Some Medinans read ālihatan hawāhu, a preposed plural second object, treating the worshiped gods as different kinds.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r8.anchor: وقرأ بعض المدنيين " آلهة هواه " جمع إله، وهو أيضا مفعول مقدم

SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r9.claim: The first object of araʾayta is man, and its second object is the interrogative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:25:43/r9.anchor: ومفعول " أرأيت " الأول " من " ، والثاني: الجملة الاستفهامية

QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#1/r1.claim: The second hamza is softened between vowels, a pronunciation identified as common in Ḥijāzī recitation.
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#1/r1.anchor: Hamza softened (tashīl) — the second hamza in raʾayta is eased between vowels

QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#2/r1.claim: A canonical variant elides the second hamza entirely to simplify the consonant cluster.
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#2/r1.anchor: Hamza dropped entirely — the second hamza is elided, simplifying the consonant cluster

QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#3/r1.claim: This variant inserts a lengthened alif before the hamza as compensatory elongation.
QIRAAT-ER:25:43:1#3/r1.anchor: Madd (elongation) inserted — a lengthened alif before the hamza; compensatory lengthening variant

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: The verb اتخذ in the verse belongs to افتعل: this pattern begins with tāʾ after a connecting hamza and follows the same inflectional scheme as انفعل.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: انفعل begins with nūn and requires a connecting alif at the start; its present and participial forms follow ينفعل, منفعل, and منفعل with the stated participle vowel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: أما النون فتلحق أولا ساكنة فتلزمها ألف الوصل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: The nūn prefix occurs only in انفعل; the tāʾ in second position belongs only to افتعل when the preceding consonant is part of the root.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: ولا تلحق النون أولا إلا في انفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: استفعل starts with sīn and tāʾ and takes a connecting alif; its present form is يستفعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: وتلحق السين أولا والتاء بعدها ثم تسكن السين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: Across augmented patterns, the present vowel before the final consonant usually distinguishes active and passive forms; patterns with open vowels such as يتفاعل and يتفعل retain them.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: كسرة الحرف الذي قبل آخر حرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: Forms with a connecting alif generally follow فعِل in movement and sukūn, except that the third consonant is ḍamma; examples include استفعل and افتعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: من جميع هذه الأفعال التي لحقتها ألف الوصل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: The pattern افعاللت parallels استفعل in inflection, but idghām causes its first lām to be vowelless; its alif changes to wāw when deriving the cited form because of the preceding ḍamma.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: افعللت parallels افتعل in conjugation and is likewise affected by idghām; احمررت illustrates the only position where a doubled lām follows a vowelled consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: ويكون الحرف افعللت فيجري مجرى افتعلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: افعوعلت inserts wāw between two عين consonants and follows استفعل in conjugation; the separation occurs only in this pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: ويفصل بين العينين بواو ويسكن أول حرف فيلزمه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: افعولت adds a doubled wāw in the third position and also follows استفعل in inflection, as in اعلوط and اعلوطت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: وتلحق الواو ثالثة مضاعفة ويسكن أول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: The forms هرقت and أهرقت reflect substitution or compensation for the hamza; in أهرقت the hāʾ compensates for deleting and vowellessing the root عين.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: وأما هرقت وهرحت فأبدلوا مكان الهمزة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.claim: أَسْطَاعَ similarly uses sīn as a compensatory added consonant, since sīn is among the verbal augment letters; the added hāʾ is also licensed in verbs.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتسكنأوائلهمنالأفعالالم.anchor: ونظير هذا قولهم أسطاع يسطيع جعلوا العوض السين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r1.claim: The question invites the Prophet to marvel at their ugly conduct after their speech, actions, and fate have been described.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r1.anchor: تعجب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من شناعة حالهم بعد حكاية قبائحهم من الأقوال والأفعال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r2.claim: Ra'ayta is visual seeing; man is its object and a relative pronoun whose following clause is its relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن رأى بصرية و ( من ) مفعولها وهي اسم موصول والجملة بعدها صلة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r3.claim: Ittakhadha takes two objects: desire is the first and his god the second, with the second object advanced.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r3.anchor: و ( اتخذ ) متعدية لمفعولين أولهما ( هواه ) وثانيهما ( إلهه ) وقدم على الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r4.claim: The person makes desire a god by obeying it and basing religion on it, turning from compelling evidence and clear proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r4.anchor: أي أرأيت الذي جعل هواه إلها لنفسه بأن أطاعه وبنى عليه أمر دينه معرضا عن استماع الحجة الباهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r5.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r5.claim: Ibn al-Munir says advancing the second object gives an exclusive sense: the person has made nothing but desire his deity.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r5.anchor: وقال ابن المنير في تقديم المفعول الثاني هنا نكتة حسنة وهي إفادة الحصر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r6.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r6.claim: Al-Fara'id rejects Ibn al-Munir's analogy, arguing that with two definite nouns whichever comes first is the subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r6.anchor: وقال صاحب الفرائد : تقديم المفعول الثاني يمكن حيث يمكن تقديم الخبر على المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r7.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r7.claim: Al-Fara'id says advancing his god signals the person necessarily has a deity, not a servant, as in the example about a son and servant.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r7.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : المتقدم ههنا يشعر بالثبات بخلاف المتأخر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r8.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r8.claim: Al-Tibi says the deity is the original comparison and desire the likeness; fronting it depicts desire as more deserving of worship, as in 2:275.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r8.anchor: لأنهم نزلوا أهواءهم في المتابعة منزلة الاله

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r9.speaker: المفتاح
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r9.claim: Al-Tibi notes that the author of al-Miftah alluded to this rhetorical meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23/r9.anchor: ولمح صاحب المفتاح إلى هذا المعنى في كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r1.claim: Al-Fara'id illustrates the construction as making one's son a servant like a household worker, or one's servant a pampered son.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r1.anchor: صاحب الفرائد فمعنى قوله : اتخذ ابنه غلامه جعل ابنه كالغلام يخدمه في مهنة أهله

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r2.claim: The predicate is إلهه, determined by the rational context; no special semantic fronting analysis is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r2.anchor: القرينة هنا قائمة على أن ( الهه ) الخبر وهي عقلية لأن المعنى على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r3.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r3.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the second object denotes the newly assumed state, answering Abu Hayyan's insistence on fixed order between two definite nouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r3.anchor: وقال شيخ الاسلام : من توهم أنهما على الترتيب بناء على تساويهما في التعريف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r4.speaker: بعض المدنيين
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r4.claim: Some Medinans read ءالهة with tanwin as a plural and construe reversed order: each kind of desire becomes a deity.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r4.anchor: عن بعض المدنيين أنه قرأ ( ءالهة ) منونة على الجمع وجعل على التقديم والتأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r5.speaker: ابن هرمز
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r5.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads الهة on the faʿāla pattern, with reversed order: desire is made an object of worship, and the ending is intensive and declinable.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r5.anchor: أن ابن هرمز قرأ ( الهة ) على وزن فعالة وهو أيضا من التقديم والتأخير أي جعل هواه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r6.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r6.claim: Al-Lawami reports an analysis of al-ilaha as the sun and a dialectal ألاهة as a feminine proper name; the author dismisses this account as implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r6.anchor: قاله صاحب اللوامح وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r7.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who worshiped each stone he fancied and replaced it when he found a better one.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r7.anchor: والآية نزلت على ما قيل في الحرث بن قيس السهمي كان كلما هوى حجرا عبده

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that a pre-Islamic man worshiped a white stone until he found a better one, then discarded it and worshiped the replacement.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال : كان الرجل يعبد الحجر الأبيض رمانا من الدهر في الجاهلية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r9.claim: The reports do not require interpreting هواه as the thing desired (his object of desire).
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r9.anchor: وزعم بعضهم لهذا ونحوه أن هواه بمعنى مهويه وليس بلازم كما لايخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase broadly: a person acted on whatever he wanted or desired, unchecked by scruple or piety.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في الآية كلما هوى شيئا ركبه وكلما اشتهى شيئا أتاه لايحجزه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r11.claim: The verse includes both worshiping something besides God at the prompting of desire and following desire in other sins; this is the scope implied by al-Hasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r11.anchor: فالآية شاملة لمن عبد غير الله تعالى حسب هواه ولمن أطاع الهوى في سائر المعاصي وهو الذي يقتضيه كلام الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says there is shirk among the qibla people: a hypocrite may prostrate to the sun or moon and worship desire; he treats hypocrites as sinners.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r12.anchor: عبد بن حميد أنه قيل له : أفي أهل القبلة شرك فقال : نعم المنافق مشرك يسجد للشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r13.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r13.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying that following desire is among the gravest objects of worship beneath heaven; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r13.anchor: أبي أمامة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما تحت ظل السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r14.claim: The verse's full scope is avoided only by following what God chose and legislated in all matters; unbelievers are included especially clearly.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p23#2/r14.anchor: ولا يكاد يسلم على هذا من عموم الآية إلا من اتبع ما اختاره الله تعالى لعباده وشرعه سبحانه لهم في كل ما يأتي ويذر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r1.claim: The question rules out the Prophet acting as guardian over this person, restraining and guiding him by choice or compulsion; it rebukes this notion after his excessive devotion to desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r1.anchor: استئناف مسوق لاستبعاد كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم حفيظا على هذا المتخذ يزجره عما هو عليه من الضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r2.claim: An alternative takes رأى as cognitive and this clause as its second object, but the author finds that analysis unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24/r2.anchor: أن تكون رأي علمية وهذ الجملة في موضع المفعول الثاني وليس بذاك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r11.claim: A polytheist might worship a stone, then replace it with a stone he liked better and worship the new one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r11.anchor: وذلك أن الرجل من المشركين كان يعبد الحجر فإذا رأى حجرا أحسن منه طرح الأول وأخذ الآخر فعبده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas describes one who abandons worship of God and follows desire to worship a stone, asking what his state would be before God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أرأيت من ترك عبادة الله وخالقه ثم هوي حجرا فعبده ما حاله عندي؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r13.claim: A wakīl is a guardian; the Prophet cannot be responsible for protecting such a person from following desire and worshipping what he wants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r13.anchor: أي: حافظا، يقول: أفأنت عليه كفيل تحفظه من اتباع هواه وعبادة من يهوى من دون الله؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r14.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r14.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r8.claim: God comforts the Prophet, who grieves because he earnestly wants his people to return to what benefits them and avoid harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r8.anchor: وكان ذلك مما يحزنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لشدة حرصه على رجوعهم , ولزوم ما ينفعهم واجتناب ما يضرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r9.claim: They reduce god to desire and serve only passion, without a rational basis for idol-worship that could make them leave it; only God can turn such desires aside.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r9.anchor: فهم لا يعبدون إلا الهوى , وهو ميل الشهوة ورمي النفس إلى الشيء , لا شبهة لهم أصلا في عبادة الأصنام يرجعون عنها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a pre-Islamic man might worship a white stone, then replace it with a better-looking stone and worship the new one.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r1.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r2.claim: A similar account of changing the stone worshipped is also reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person as a disbeliever who follows desire without God's guidance or proof; God led him astray according to prior knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r3.anchor: ابن عباس : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه قال : ذلك الكافر

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r4.claim: Hasan al-Basri says such a person follows anything he desires.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r4.anchor: الحسن : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه قال : لا يهوي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r5.claim: Hasan also describes a hypocrite who makes desire his god and acts on whatever he wants.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r5.anchor: الحسن في قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r6.claim: Qatada says the person does everything he desires, restrained by neither scruple nor piety.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r6.anchor: قتادة قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2699#2/r7.claim: Qatada glosses wakīl as a supporter or helper.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r1.claim: The verse consoles the Prophet over repeated rejection despite his eagerness to guide them: people who make desire their deity are not expected to find guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r1.anchor: استئناف خوطب به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يخطر بنفسه من الحزن على تكرر إعراضهم عن دعوته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r2.claim: اتخذ takes two objects as a causative verb, closer to كسا and أعطى than to ظن; the first object is transformed into the state named by the second.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r2.anchor: إلى باب كسا وأعطى أقرب منه إلى باب ظن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r3.claim: On the unadvanced object order, a person makes the thing he desires to worship his deity; idolaters worship idols from appetite rather than proof of their right to worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r3.anchor: ومعناه منقول عن سعيد بن جبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r4.speaker: ابن عرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r4.claim: Ibn Arfa chose the ordinary-order interpretation as the sole correct one; Ibn Ashur says his categorical judgment is not convincing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r5.claim: With the second object advanced, the person makes desire his guide, acting only in accord with appetite; desire is then like a deity through his obedience to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r5.anchor: من اتخذ هواه قدوة له في أعماله لا يأتي عملا إلا إذا كان وفاقا لشهوته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r6.claim: In the advanced-object reading, calling desire a deity is an emphatic metaphor: it resembles a god in the obedience it receives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p34#2/r6.anchor: شبيها بإلهه في إطاعته على طريقة التشبيه البليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is associated with the broader reading that a person follows desire as a deity; it condemns idolatry and other wrongs and indecencies.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف وابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf's author and Ibn Atiyya also adopt the broader reading of following desire as a deity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r3.claim: Both object-order interpretations should be understood as intended meanings of the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r3.anchor: وكلا المعنيين ينبغي أن يكون محملا للآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r4.claim: If the two clauses form one connected construction, رأيت means cognitive knowledge, the first question is rhetorical denial, and the second clause supplies the omitted second object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r4.anchor: كلاما واحدا متصلا ثانيه بأوله اتصال المفعول بعامله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r5.claim: In the connected construction, the interrogative suspends رأيت from taking its object; the second clause substitutes for that object, so one does not pause at هواه.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r5.anchor: الفعل معلق عن العمل فيه بسبب الاستفهام على نحو قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r6.claim: In the connected reading, the first question gives an overview and the second elaborates it; the second interrogative reinforces the first, as in 17:49.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r7.claim: Alternatively, each clause is syntactically independent: the first question expresses astonished, mixed disapproval, and the فاء makes the second clause follow from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r7.anchor: مستعملا في التعجيب من حال الذين اتخذوا إلههم هواهم تعجيبا مشوبا بالإنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r8.claim: On the independent-clause reading, the second question denies that the Prophet can pull someone out of error, continuing the point in 25:42.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p35/r8.anchor: إنك لا تستطيع قلعه عن ضلاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r1.claim: من refers to the group described as seeing the punishment in 25:42; its attached pronouns remain singular by agreement with the word-form من.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r1.anchor: على الجمع المتحدث عنه في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r2.claim: The plural sense is either people who made desire a deity or people who took deities for the sake of desire; إله can be a generic singular for several gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r2.anchor: اتخذوا هواهم إلها لهم أو من اتخذوا آلهة لأجل هواهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r3.claim: Putting أنت before the verbal predicate emphasizes that the Prophet cannot serve as their keeper in a way that makes them believe by persistent calling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى إنكار ما حمل الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام نفسه من الحرص والحزن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r4.claim: The point that the Prophet cannot compel people to believe parallels 10:99.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p36/r4.anchor: أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r1.claim: The Prophet is made to marvel at their ignorance in worshipping whatever their desire calls them to worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r1.anchor: ثم عجب نبيه من جهلهم حين عبدوا ما دعاهم إليه الهوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a man would worship a stone, then discard it for another stone he found more attractive.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس كان أحدهم يعبد الحجر فاذا رأى ماهو أحسن منه رمى به وعبد الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says it is the unbeliever who acts on anything he desires.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة هو الكافر لا يهوى شيئا إلا ركبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the person follows desire and abandons truth, making desire function as a god.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة المعنى يتبع هواه ويدع الحق فهو له كالإله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r5.claim: A wakīl here would be a guardian who protects him from following his desire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r5.anchor: أي حفيظا يحفظه من اتباع هواه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r6.speaker: الكلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī alleges that this verse was abrogated by the fighting verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#3/r6.anchor: وزعم الكلبي ان هذه الآية منسوخة بآية القتال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r4.claim: The following verse warns the Prophet that no one can guide a person whom God has decreed wretched and astray except God Himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r4.anchor: من كتب الله عليه الشقاوة والضلال، فإنه لا يهديه أحد إلا الله

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r8.claim: One explanation says a person makes whatever he desires into a god, like an idolater who discards one stone image for a better-looking one.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r8.anchor: قيل: جعل إلهه ما يهواه، وهو غاية الجهل، وكان الرجل من المشركين يعبد الحجر والصنم، فإن رأى أحسن منه رمى به، وأخذ الآخر فعبده

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r9.claim: Another explanation says they follow desire as they follow gods, so desire is effectively treated and worshipped as a god.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r9.anchor: وقيل: اتبع هواه كاتباع الآلهة، فكأنه اتخذه إلها وعبده

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says الهوى here means what unbelievers worship besides God.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الهوى ما يعبدون من دون الله

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r11.claim: One gloss asks whether Muhammad can guard them from falsehood despite their ignorance and heedlessness.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r11.anchor: قيل: حافظا لهم عن الباطل مع هذا الجهل والغفلة الذي هم فيه

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r12.claim: Another gloss says the Prophet is not responsible for making them believe; his duty is only to convey.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r12.anchor: قيل: ليس عليك أن يؤمنوا إنما عليك البلاغ

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.claim: The verses show human actions are originated by people: the cited actions and refusals require a choosing agent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says some people worshipped a stone they admired, then abandoned it for a more attractive one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنهم قوم كان الرجل منهم يعبد حجرا يستحسنه , فإذا رأى أحسن منه عبده وترك الأول , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r2.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r2.claim: Al-Naqqash identifies the person as al-Harith ibn Qays, who worshipped whatever he desired.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه الحارث بن قيس كان إذا هوى شيئا عبده , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada explain the phrase as following one's desire in everything it calls one to do.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه الذي يتبع هواه في كل ما دعا إليه , قاله الحسن , وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r4.claim: Qatada glosses wakīl as a supporter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r4.anchor: أحدها : يعني ناصرا , قاله قتادة . الثاني : حفيظا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r5.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Salam glosses wakīl as a guardian.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r5.anchor: الثاني : حفيظا , قاله يحيى بن سلام . الثالث : كفيلا
