MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses wakīl as a guarantor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r6.anchor: الثالث : كفيلا قاله الكلبي . الرابع : مسيطرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146/r7.claim: Al-Suddi glosses wakīl as one who exercises control.

MUQATIL:25:41-43/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r5.speaker: الحارث بن قيس السهمى
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r5.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who desired something and worshipped it.
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r5.anchor: وذلك أن الحارث بن قيس السهمى هوى شيئا فعبده

MUQATIL:25:41-43/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r6.claim: Muhammad is not a controller over such a person; the Prophet wants to change the person’s choice between guidance and error.
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r6.anchor: يعنى مسيطرا يقول: تريد أن تبدل المشيئة إلى الهدى والضلالة.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r1.claim: Anyone who follows desire in what they do or leave undone worships desire and makes it their god.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r1.anchor: أى من أطاع هواه فيما يأتى ويذر فهو عابد هواه وجاعله الهه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r2.claim: The rhetorical question asks how the Prophet could call someone who recognizes only desire as a god to guidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r2.anchor: هذا الذى لا يرى معبودا الا هواه كيف تستطيع ان تدعوه إلى الهدى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r3.claim: A report says a pre-Islamic man worshipped a stone, then replaced it with a better-looking stone when he passed one.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r3.anchor: يروى أن الواحد من أهل الجاهلية كان يعبد الحجر فاذا مر بحجر أحسن منه ترك الأول وعبد الثانى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r4.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r4.claim: Al-Hasan applies the verse to every person who follows their own desire.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن هو فى كل متع هواه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r5.claim: The Prophet is no guardian commissioned to turn such a person from desire to guidance; his role is only to convey the message.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#3/r5.anchor: أى حفيظا تحفظه من متابعة هواه وعبادة ما يهواه أفأنت تكون عليه موكلا

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r1.claim: God tells the Prophet to marvel that they persist in shirk despite acknowledging Him as creator and provider, then worship a stone without proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r1.anchor: عجب نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من إضمارهم على الشرك وإصرارهم عليه مع إقرارهم بأنه خالقهم ورازقهم

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and others say an Arab who desired something worshipped it, then abandoned it for a better-looking object; the preposition is omitted and the sense is “a god according to his desire.”
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي وغيره: كانت العرب إذا هوي الرجل منهم شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says desire itself is an idol worshipped apart from God, and recited the verse as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الهوى إله يعبد من دون الله

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r4.claim: Another view means he obeys his desire; al-Ḥasan says he follows anything he desires, which Qurtubi regards as the same sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r4.anchor: وقيل: { اتخذ إلهه هواه } أي أطاع هواه

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r5.claim: An anonymous poem imagines an ascetic praying to a woman before praying to God, illustrating desire redirecting worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r5.anchor: لصلى لها قبل الصلاة لربه ولا ارتد في الدنيا بأعمال فاتك

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r6.claim: A wakīl would guard or guarantee a return to faith and rescue from corruption; guidance is not the Prophet’s choice, whose duty is to convey.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r6.anchor: أي حفيظا وكفيلا حتى ترده إلى الإيمان وتخرجه من هذا الفساد

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r7.claim: Qurtubi calls the passage a rebuttal to the Qadariyya.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r8.claim: One view says the verse was abrogated by the fighting verse; another says it remains as consolation for the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:43/r8.anchor: ثم قيل: إنها منسوخة بآية القتال
